purpose: machine-readable expert system to design inquiry, establish validity, and judge knowledge claims as a node in a knowledge-searcher meta-KB for finding and validating authoritative knowledge
assumptions: no observed dataset, expert judgment, or experimental evidence was supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
domain spans research design, philosophy of science, and measurement/validity at the intersection used for knowledge discovery
scores are relative ordering priors, not measured quantities
the KB is consumed by a meta-KB knowledge searcher, so outputs are scoped, graded knowledge claims
exclusions: domain-specific subject-matter content (e.g., a particular biology or economics finding)
institutional ethics-board procedures beyond feasibility flags
qualitative-only methodologies are treated only via construct and validity lenses, not as a separate track

competency_questions.question: Does the inquiry account for prior evidence and already-known validity threats?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

glossary.definition: degree to which a design supports an unconfounded causal inference for the studied sample
degree to which a finding generalizes across populations, settings, and times
degree to which a measure represents the intended theoretical construct
property of a claim that some observation could in principle refute it
a common cause of treatment and outcome that biases the effect estimate
the precisely defined quantity a study aims to estimate
the status of a conjecture that has survived severe tests, not a probability of truth
property that a measure functions equivalently across groups

evidence_label_policy.rule: all estimates are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR; observed_impact, data_quality, and observed_co_occurrence are 0.0 with no observed dataset

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors over research-methodology and epistemology structure, weights, and risks

nodes.definition: Specify the research question, knowledge claim type, and inquiry paradigm before any design or measurement choices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: question reframed after pilot evidence or scope drift detected

pros.example: an exploratory vs confirmatory split changes the entire design

cons.claim: premature framing can lock a wrong question
cons.example: fixing question before literature scan biases design

failure_modes: claim type misclassified as causal when descriptive

nodes.definition: Aggregate and appraise prior knowledge to position the claim and identify validity threats already known.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new high-quality study contradicts the synthesized evidence map

pros.example: known confounders documented before design

cons.example: null results missing distort prior

nodes.definition: Apply demarcation criteria to judge whether a claim is scientifically testable versus non-falsifiable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hypothesis revised so that it becomes unfalsifiable or newly testable

pros.example: an unfalsifiable hypothesis is rejected before funding

cons.example: Duhem-Quine: tests never hit one hypothesis alone

failure_modes: treating ad hoc rescue as corroboration
conflating absence of evidence with falsification

nodes.definition: Design risky predictions whose refutation would disconfirm the conjecture and whose survival yields corroboration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a severe test refutes a previously corroborated prediction

pros.claim: prioritizes severe tests over easy confirmations
pros.example: a bold novel prediction tested beats a safe one

cons.claim: corroboration is not probability of truth
cons.example: high corroboration can still precede refutation

nodes.definition: Locate the inquiry within a paradigm and assess normal-science assumptions and incommensurability risks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a paradigm shift reframes which anomalies count as evidence

pros.claim: explains why rival frameworks talk past each other
pros.example: incommensurable measures block direct comparison

cons.example: claiming incommensurability to dodge falsification

nodes.definition: Select an experimental or quasi-experimental design matched to the causal claim and feasibility constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feasibility constraint forces a switch from experimental to quasi-experimental design

pros.example: RCT chosen when randomization is ethical and feasible

cons.claim: strongest design may be infeasible or unethical
cons.example: randomizing harmful exposure is not permissible

failure_modes: design cannot identify the target estimand
acceptance_tests: design supports the stated causal claim

nodes.definition: Implement randomized allocation (including factorial structure) to remove systematic confounding in treatment assignment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: balance check reveals failed randomization or attrition imbalance

pros.claim: randomization neutralizes known and unknown confounders
pros.example: balanced arms support unbiased ATE estimation

cons.claim: external validity may suffer in artificial settings
cons.example: tightly controlled trial generalizes poorly

nodes.definition: Apply quasi-experimental identification (RDD, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables) when randomization is unavailable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an identifying assumption (parallel trends, exclusion restriction) is violated

pros.example: DiD exploits a policy change as natural experiment

cons.example: exclusion restriction cannot be fully verified

nodes.definition: Identify and control confounders threatening internal validity through design or analytic adjustment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a previously unmeasured confounder is discovered

pros.claim: protects internal validity of causal claim
pros.example: adjusting for confounder removes spurious association

cons.claim: adjusting for colliders or mediators induces bias
cons.example: conditioning on a collider opens a backdoor path

acceptance_tests: confounder set justified by a causal graph
adjustment does not condition on colliders

nodes.definition: Assess whether the design supports a causal inference free of confounding and selection bias for the studied sample.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a threat to internal validity is reclassified as material

pros.claim: is the precondition for any causal claim
pros.example: without internal validity an effect estimate is meaningless

cons.claim: can be over-optimized at cost of generalizability
cons.example: lab-perfect control yields non-transportable result

acceptance_tests: each Campbell threat addressed or documented
causal claim restricted to identified estimand

nodes.definition: Assess generalizability and transportability of findings across populations, settings, and times.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: replication in a new setting fails to reproduce the effect

pros.claim: determines whether results inform decisions elsewhere
pros.example: scope conditions tell users where a finding applies

cons.claim: trades off against tight internal control
cons.example: broad sampling reintroduces confounding noise

nodes.definition: Ensure operationalized measures faithfully represent the intended theoretical constructs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measure is shown to capture a different construct than intended

pros.claim: prevents measuring the wrong thing well
pros.example: a valid scale beats a precise but mis-targeted one

cons.claim: constructs can be underspecified or contested
cons.example: latent construct definitions vary across theories

acceptance_tests: measure maps to a defined construct

nodes.definition: Test whether a measure behaves equivalently across groups so comparisons reflect true differences, not measurement artifacts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: invariance test fails for a key comparison group

pros.example: scalar invariance permits comparing latent means

cons.claim: strict invariance is rarely fully met
cons.example: partial invariance complicates interpretation

nodes.definition: Define sampling frame, recruitment, and power so the design can detect the target effect within the scope conditions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed effect size differs from the power-analysis assumption

pros.example: adequate power avoids false-negative conclusions

cons.example: wrong effect-size guess invalidates the power calc

nodes.definition: Specify instruments, procedures, and reliability checks that produce trustworthy raw data.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reliability falls below threshold in pilot

pros.example: calibrated protocol yields reproducible data

cons.example: over-standardization loses ecological nuance

nodes.definition: Pre-specify hypotheses, design, and analysis to separate confirmatory from exploratory inference and curb researcher degrees of freedom.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deviation from the preregistered plan is required

pros.example: preregistered analysis fixes the test before data

cons.example: rigid plan blocks unanticipated but valid analyses

nodes.definition: Estimate the target estimand with an estimator consistent with the design and stated assumptions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: estimator assumptions violated by observed data distribution

pros.claim: links design to a defensible numeric claim
pros.example: estimator matched to design recovers the estimand

cons.example: wrong SE assumption understates uncertainty

nodes.definition: Quality-check inference for multiplicity, robustness, and overclaiming before any knowledge claim is asserted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a robustness check overturns the headline result

pros.example: robustness across specs supports a stronger claim

cons.claim: excessive correction can hide real effects
cons.example: over-conservative thresholds raise false negatives

nodes.definition: Assess reproducibility and replicability to judge the durability of a knowledge claim.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an independent replication fails to reproduce the finding

pros.example: successful replication raises claim confidence

cons.example: replication budgets limit coverage of claims

nodes.definition: Grade the strength of accumulated evidence and assign a justified confidence level to the knowledge claim.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence shifts the grade across a confidence threshold

pros.claim: makes claim confidence explicit and auditable
pros.example: a graded claim communicates uncertainty honestly

cons.example: different rubrics yield different grades

nodes.definition: Assert the final, scope-bounded knowledge claim with its evidence grade, validity caveats, and falsification status.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-publication evidence refutes or materially revises the claim

pros.example: a scoped graded claim is reusable by downstream KBs

cons.example: retraction is costly once a claim is published

acceptance_tests: claim restricted to identified estimand and scope

edges.benefit_of_coupling: focused search reuses the question scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: drift if framing changes after search
edges.example: a reframed question forces re-running the search
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; rerun synthesis on reframe

edges.why_related: claim type determines the demarcation test
edges.benefit_of_coupling: testability judged against the framed claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatch if claim type is wrong
edges.example: a causal claim type triggers falsifiability testing
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; demarcation re-evaluated on reframe

edges.why_related: only testable claims get risky predictions
edges.example: a falsifiable hypothesis yields a severe test
edges.resolution_rule: demarcation dominates; no predictions for unfalsifiable claims

edges.example: the evidence map reveals the dominant paradigm
edges.resolution_rule: synthesis dominates; paradigm record follows the map

edges.example: a causal question rules out purely descriptive designs
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; design must serve the claim

edges.example: documented confounders favor a stronger design
edges.resolution_rule: synthesis dominates; design must address known threats

edges.example: an RCT choice triggers an allocation protocol
edges.resolution_rule: design dominates; randomization only if design supports it

edges.example: a DiD choice triggers parallel-trends checks
edges.resolution_rule: design dominates; identification strategy follows design

edges.benefit_of_coupling: control plan builds on randomized balance
edges.example: balanced arms still need attrition-confounding checks
edges.resolution_rule: randomization dominates; control plan adjusts residuals

edges.example: IV strategy requires controlling for instrument validity threats
edges.resolution_rule: identification dominates; control plan enforces assumptions

edges.risk_of_conflict: invalid causal claim if control fails
edges.example: an unaddressed confounder lowers the internal-validity verdict
edges.resolution_rule: control dominates; verdict reflects residual threats

edges.example: an internally invalid effect cannot be generalized
edges.resolution_rule: internal validity dominates; no generalization without it

edges.why_related: the claim defines constructs to operationalize
edges.example: a construct in the question must be operationalized
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; constructs follow the claim

edges.why_related: a defined construct precedes invariance testing
edges.risk_of_conflict: comparing groups on a shifting construct
edges.example: a cross-group comparison requires invariance testing
edges.resolution_rule: construct definition dominates; invariance tested after

edges.why_related: design dictates sampling and power needs
edges.example: a factorial design raises the required sample size
edges.resolution_rule: design dominates; power plan follows design

edges.example: a defined construct yields a calibrated instrument
edges.resolution_rule: construct dominates; protocol implements it

edges.why_related: design must be fixed before preregistration
edges.example: a finalized design is registered with its analysis plan
edges.resolution_rule: design dominates; prereg locks the design

edges.risk_of_conflict: HARKing if controls chosen post hoc
edges.example: the covariate set is registered before data
edges.resolution_rule: control dominates; prereg fixes the adjustment set

edges.example: the preregistered estimator is applied to data
edges.resolution_rule: prereg dominates; deviations must be disclosed

edges.example: low reliability widens the effect interval
edges.resolution_rule: protocol dominates; estimation flags unreliable inputs

edges.benefit_of_coupling: QA reuses the estimate and plan
edges.example: a single estimate is stress-tested for robustness
edges.resolution_rule: estimation dominates input; QA gates the claim

edges.why_related: calibrated claims define what to replicate
edges.example: a robust claim is targeted for direct replication
edges.resolution_rule: QA dominates; replication follows calibration

edges.example: specification sensitivity lowers the evidence grade
edges.resolution_rule: QA dominates; grade reflects robustness

edges.example: a failed replication downgrades the evidence
edges.resolution_rule: replication dominates; grade reflects reproducibility

edges.why_related: the grade bounds the assertable claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: claim reuses the grade and caveats
edges.example: a low grade restricts the claim to tentative
edges.resolution_rule: grading dominates; claim cannot exceed the grade

edges.example: narrow scope conditions restrict the claim's reach
edges.resolution_rule: external validity dominates; claim carries scope caveats

edges.why_related: internal validity verdict gates any causal claim
edges.example: a weak verdict downgrades the claim to associational
edges.resolution_rule: internal validity dominates; causal language requires it

edges.why_related: falsification status is part of the claim record
edges.example: a non-falsifiable claim is labeled non-scientific
edges.resolution_rule: demarcation dominates; status attached to claim

edges.why_related: tight internal control trades off generalizability
edges.benefit_of_coupling: naming the tradeoff guides design balance
edges.example: lab control improves internal validity but narrows transportability
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize internal validity for causal claims; document scope limits explicitly

edges.why_related: strict randomized settings can be unrepresentative
edges.example: a placebo-controlled efficacy trial generalizes poorly to practice
edges.resolution_rule: keep randomization; add pragmatic or replication arms to recover external validity

edges.why_related: rigid prereg can block valid unanticipated analyses
edges.example: an unexpected nonlinearity is barred by a strict registered linear model
edges.resolution_rule: follow prereg for confirmatory tests; report deviations as clearly-labeled exploratory analyses

edges.benefit_of_coupling: flagging it reconciles Popperian and grading views
edges.example: a corroborated theory is graded as if confirmed, overstating certainty
edges.resolution_rule: treat corroboration as non-falsification, not proof; grade caps below certainty

edges.example: an existing validated scale is adopted from the literature
edges.resolution_rule: prefer literature-grounded constructs; justify any new operationalization

edges.why_related: paradigm context frames how the claim is communicated
edges.example: a claim is stated relative to its paradigm's assumptions
edges.resolution_rule: attach paradigm assumptions to the claim; avoid cross-paradigm overreach

edges.why_related: sample size and structure bound estimator precision
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sizing the sample bounds the achievable interval
edges.example: a small clustered sample widens the confidence interval
edges.resolution_rule: estimation must respect the sampling structure; report power limits

edges.example: failed scalar invariance restricts cross-country generalization
edges.resolution_rule: limit generalization to groups with established invariance

edges.why_related: failed replication can trigger design reconsideration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: closing the loop improves future designs
edges.example: a non-replication prompts revisiting the identification strategy
edges.resolution_rule: trigger redesign only on material non-replication; stop after one documented design revision per claim

edges.why_related: robustness failures can reveal missed confounders
edges.example: a sensitivity check exposes an omitted confounder
edges.resolution_rule: revisit control once when QA flags a confounder; stop after the adjustment plan is updated and re-validated

edges.why_related: a refuted claim can reopen the inquiry framing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: closing the loop seeds the next study
edges.example: post-publication refutation reopens the research question
edges.resolution_rule: reopen framing only on material refutation; stop after one reframing cycle per refutation

conflict_axes.trigger: design tightening improves control but narrows generalizability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: internal validity dominates for causal claims; external validity is recovered via scope conditions and replication
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when a decision requires generalizing a tightly controlled effect to a high-stakes population
conflict_axes.example: an efficacy RCT result is applied to routine practice without scope caveats

conflict_axes.trigger: strict randomized conditions reduce ecological realism
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: preserve randomization for identification; add pragmatic arms or replication for realism
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when stakeholders demand real-world applicability from an artificial trial
conflict_axes.example: a placebo-controlled trial under-represents real adherence patterns

conflict_axes.trigger: a locked analysis plan blocks a valid unanticipated analysis
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: confirmatory tests follow the preregistration; new analyses are reported as labeled exploratory
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when an unplanned but theory-relevant pattern emerges in the data
conflict_axes.example: a registered linear model misses a clear nonlinearity

conflict_axes.trigger: Popperian corroboration resists being read as confirmation in a grading rubric
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: treat corroboration as survived-refutation, not proof; grades cap below certainty
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when a corroborated theory is communicated as established fact
conflict_axes.example: a long-corroborated theory is later refuted, exposing overclaimed grading

conflict_axes.trigger: adequate power demands a sample the design cannot feasibly recruit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: power requirements bound design ambition; downgrade claim scope rather than run underpowered
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when recruitment cannot reach the power-required sample size
conflict_axes.example: an underpowered trial yields an inconclusive null

conflict_axes.trigger: a precise instrument may not represent the intended construct
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: construct fidelity dominates; precision is useless if it measures the wrong thing
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when a reliable instrument shows poor convergent validity
conflict_axes.example: a highly reliable scale measures a different latent trait

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to assert a claim conflicts with robustness and replication checks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rigor dominates assertion; a claim may not be asserted before QA gates pass
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when a deadline pressures asserting before robustness checks complete
conflict_axes.example: a headline result is published before sensitivity analysis

conflict_axes.trigger: incentives to maximize novelty deprioritize confirming durability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: durability evidence dominates for high-stakes claims; novelty is subordinate to replicability
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when a novel claim is asserted without any replication evidence
conflict_axes.example: a single surprising study drives a strong claim that fails to replicate

edge_cases.trigger: a claim cites a node or source that does not exist
edge_cases.example: a claim references a deleted internal-validity verdict
edge_cases.detection_method: run reference-resolution over all id fields
resolution: restore or remove the dangling reference

edge_cases.trigger: a node omits a required field after edit
edge_cases.example: a node loses its score_derivation_inputs block
edge_cases.detection_method: diff each object against the required structure

edge_cases.trigger: a heuristic estimate is labeled observed without data
edge_cases.example: an evidence grade is marked observed with no dataset
edge_cases.detection_method: scan labels for observed/experimentally_validated without eligible source

edge_cases.trigger: one node bundles design, control, and estimation
edge_cases.failure_mode: oversized step cannot finish in one session
edge_cases.example: a single node tries to own design and analysis
edge_cases.detection_method: check node scope_boundary against one-session bound
resolution: split the node along scope boundaries

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests
edge_cases.example: the knowledge-claim node has no acceptance tests
edge_cases.detection_method: flag nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 and empty acceptance_tests

edge_cases.trigger: a claim is hard-locked before QA and review gates pass
edge_cases.failure_mode: premature hard lock blocks needed revision
edge_cases.example: a claim is locked before replication assessment
edge_cases.detection_method: verify lock_condition order against gate pass-state

edge_cases.example: repeated non-replications keep reopening the design
edge_cases.detection_method: count revisits against the loop stop condition

edge_cases.trigger: a tradeoff is encoded as a dependency
edge_cases.example: internal-vs-external tension is modeled as a prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: check each dependency edge for negative tension semantics
resolution: split into dependency and conflict edges

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node is prioritized before its prerequisite
the evidence map is outdated at grading time
edge_cases.failure_mode: stale source grounding misgrades the claim
edge_cases.example: a grade rests on a superseded literature search
edge_cases.detection_method: compare search date against grading date threshold

edge_cases.trigger: a step ends without its handoff artifact
edge_cases.example: a design step produces no design_choice_record
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each major step emitted its handoff artifact

edge_cases.trigger: a score uses a variable not in score_derivation_inputs
edge_cases.example: a confidence_score depends on an undocumented input
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute every score from declared inputs only

workflow.objective: scope the question and classify the claim
workflow.do_first_because: framing is the highest-coupling upstream foundation that constrains all later choices

workflow.objective: position the claim against prior knowledge and demarcation
acceptance_tests: claim is falsifiable or explicitly bounded
workflow.do_first_because: demarcation and prior-threat capture prevent designing for untestable or already-refuted claims

workflow.objective: design risky predictions for confirmatory testing
acceptance_tests: each prediction is severe and refutable
workflow.do_first_because: severe tests must be defined before data so confirmation bias cannot select easy tests

acceptance_tests: measure maps to a defined construct
workflow.do_first_because: construct definition must precede instrument and design so measures target the right thing
design is high-irreversibility and high-coupling; it gates randomization, sampling, and estimation
identification and power must be set before measurement and estimation to avoid bias and underpowering

workflow.objective: control confounding and adjudicate internal validity
workflow.do_first_because: internal validity is the precondition for any causal claim and must pass before generalization
scope conditions must be set before the claim so generalization stays bounded

workflow.objective: lock analysis plan and instruments before data
workflow.do_first_because: pre-specification separates confirmatory from exploratory and curbs p-hacking before any data is seen

workflow.objective: estimate the estimand and quality-check inference
entry_criteria: analysis plan locked and data collected
workflow.do_first_because: estimation and QA must precede grading so the grade rests on robust, non-overclaimed inference

workflow.objective: grade evidence and assert the bounded claim
acceptance_tests: claim restricted to estimand and scope
exit_criteria: final claim asserted with grade and caveats
workflow.do_first_because: the final claim is asserted only after dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass; hard lock requires version increment and change-control record

priority_rationale.notes: testability gates design and prediction work
prior threats must be known before design
lock plan before data to curb p-hacking
QA gates the claim against overclaiming

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk claim faces time pressure
dominance_rules.required_action: complete robustness and replication gates before asserting
dominance_rules.example: skip QA to publish faster is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a valuable node is unblocked but its prerequisite is incomplete
dominance_rules.example: estimating before design is locked is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic unless an eligible source supports the label
dominance_rules.example: reporting observed precision without data is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is proposed for lock before QA passes
dominance_rules.required_action: pass acceptance and robustness gates before any lock
dominance_rules.example: locking a claim before robustness checks is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses the review threshold
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk irreversible assertions
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human review before asserting
dominance_rules.example: auto-asserting a high-irreversibility claim is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a generalization is sought from an internally invalid effect
dominance_rules.required_action: establish internal validity before any external claim
dominance_rules.example: generalizing a confounded effect is disallowed

dominance_rules.required_action: preserve required structure over adding more nodes
dominance_rules.example: breaking object structure to add density is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds its supporting evidence grade
dominance_rules.required_action: cap claim strength at the evidence grade
dominance_rules.example: asserting beyond the grade is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: an unfalsifiable claim is framed persuasively
dominance_rules.example: presenting an unfalsifiable claim as scientific is disallowed

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step risks downstream rework
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence to stabilize upstream foundations first
dominance_rules.example: optimizing estimation before design lock is disallowed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not select a design before the question and claim type are fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reframing after design forces full redesign
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: design started while question still open
anti_rework_rules.example: a design is chosen for an unscoped question

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not populate nodes before competency questions are derived
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ungrounded nodes get rebuilt to answer missing questions
anti_rework_rules.example: nodes added with no question coverage

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not assign evidence labels before the source registry exists
anti_rework_rules.rationale: labels without sources must be downgraded later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an observed label with no source record
anti_rework_rules.example: a grade marked observed before registry built

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not design predictions before testability is judged
anti_rework_rules.rationale: predictions for untestable claims are wasted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: risky predictions for an unfalsifiable claim

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not build instruments before constructs are defined
anti_rework_rules.rationale: instruments for undefined constructs measure noise
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a protocol with no construct map

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not assess generalizability before internal validity
anti_rework_rules.rationale: generalizing an invalid effect must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scope assessment with no validity verdict
anti_rework_rules.example: scope conditions set before internal validity

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not analyze before the analysis plan is locked
anti_rework_rules.rationale: post-hoc analysis choices invite p-hacking and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: estimation deviates from a missing plan

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not grade evidence before inference QA passes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: grades on fragile inference get downgraded
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a grade assigned with no robustness report

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hard-lock a node before its acceptance tests pass
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before tests forces an expensive unlock
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: lock requested with failing acceptance tests

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not assert an irreversible claim before human review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: retracting an asserted claim is costly
anti_rework_rules.example: a high-stakes claim asserted without review

acceptance_tests: every failed check has an owner

iteration_protocol.detection: defect_list has more than one item
action: rank defects by risk and downstream impact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a locked or high-coupling node
action: run dependency and downstream impact analysis
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

acceptance_tests: repair does not introduce a new failed check

action: rerun structural, mathematical, and evidence checks
acceptance_tests: all mandatory checks pass or warn

action: recompute posterior_importance from the correct formula

iteration_protocol.detection: change request on a soft/hard-locked node
